question: Do you use single sign-on (SSO) to manage access to your business applications?
fix: Okta, JumpCloud, Google Workspace SSO, Microsoft Entra
why: Eliminates password reuse; centralises access control

question: Is multi-factor authentication (MFA) enforced for every employee, with no exceptions?
fix: Enforce via SSO provider or individual app settings
why: Single biggest control to prevent account takeover

question: Is MFA enforced specifically for admin and privileged accounts?
fix: Hardware key (YubiKey) recommended for admins
why: Admin accounts are primary target in breaches

question: Do you use a company-wide password manager?
fix: 1Password Teams, Bitwarden Business, Dashlane
why: Prevents password reuse and weak passwords

question: Do you have a formal process for removing access within 24 hours when someone leaves?
fix: Offboarding checklist + SSO deprovisioning
why: Ex-employee access is a leading cause of breaches

question: Do you maintain separate admin accounts distinct from daily-use accounts?
fix: Create dedicated admin accounts; never use for email/web
why: Limits blast radius if daily account is compromised

question: Do you track every SaaS application and software tool your team has access to?
fix: SaaS management tool: Torii, Zylo, or manual spreadsheet
why: Shadow IT is a blind spot in most SMBs

question: Do you conduct quarterly access reviews to confirm each person only has the access they still need?
fix: Schedule recurring calendar review with team leads
why: Permissions creep silently over time

question: Do you enforce least privilege — people only have access to what their role requires?
fix: Define role-based access groups; avoid admin by default
why: Limits damage from compromised accounts

question: Do you have a process for approving new software or tool access requests before they're granted?
fix: Simple approval workflow via email or Slack
why: Prevents uncontrolled SaaS sprawl

question: Are service accounts and shared credentials documented, rotated regularly, and not shared informally?
fix: Store in secrets manager; rotate every 90 days
why: Service accounts are often forgotten and over-privileged

question: Do you have visibility into employees using personal email to sign up for work tools?
fix: SaaS discovery tools or periodic self-reporting survey
why: Personal accounts bypass IT control and offboarding

question: Do you monitor for dormant accounts (unused 30+ days) and deactivate them?
fix: SSO provider reports; schedule monthly dormant account sweep
why: Dormant accounts are easy targets for attackers

question: Do you use conditional access policies (e.g. block logins from unexpected countries)?
fix: Available in Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace
why: Stops credential-stuffing attacks from offshore

question: Do you have a privileged access management (PAM) solution for sensitive systems?
fix: CyberArk, BeyondTrust, or open-source Teleport
why: Critical for companies with sensitive databases or infra

question: Do you require re-authentication for sensitive systems after a period of inactivity?
fix: Configure session timeout in SSO / app settings
why: Limits risk from unattended sessions

question: Do you log and audit all privileged account activity?
fix: CloudTrail (AWS), Azure Monitor, or SIEM tool
why: Privileged actions must be auditable

question: Have you tested your offboarding process in the last 6 months to verify access is fully removed?
fix: Run a test offboarding on a fictitious or past employee
why: Most companies assume offboarding works; many don't

question: Do all employees receive a unique username and password — no shared logins for any system?
fix: Enforce unique credentials in all application settings
why: Shared credentials prevent accountability and breach attribution

question: Are contractor and consultant accounts issued on a time-limited basis and auto-expired?
fix: Set account expiry date at creation; review weekly
why: Contractor accounts are routinely left active after engagement ends

question: Do you use phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2/WebAuthn/hardware keys) for your highest-risk accounts?
fix: YubiKey, Google Titan, or FIDO2 passkeys via Okta/Entra
why: TOTP and SMS MFA can be bypassed via SIM swap or real-time phishing

question: Is there a formal joiner process that provisions access based on role before day one?
fix: Automated provisioning via SSO with role templates
why: Inconsistent onboarding creates gaps and excess permissions from day one

question: Can you produce an access report for any employee showing all their permissions within one hour?
fix: IGA tools: SailPoint, Saviynt, or custom SSO reporting
why: Auditors and incident responders require this capability on demand

question: Do you use just-in-time (JIT) access for privileged operations rather than standing admin rights?
fix: Implement JIT via PIM in Azure AD or CyberArk
why: Standing admin access dramatically increases risk window

question: Do you have break-glass emergency accounts with tightly controlled access and full audit logging?
fix: Create sealed emergency admin account; store credentials in a vault
why: Emergency access without controls becomes a persistent backdoor

question: Are all API tokens, OAuth grants, and machine identities inventoried and reviewed quarterly?
fix: GitHub token audit, OAuth review in IdP, secrets manager inventory
why: Machine identities now outnumber human accounts 45:1 in most orgs

question: Do all company devices have endpoint detection and response (EDR) or antivirus software?
fix: CrowdStrike, SentinelOne, Microsoft Defender for Business
why: Essential first line of malware defence

question: Are all company devices encrypted (full-disk encryption enabled)?
fix: BitLocker (Windows), FileVault (Mac) — enable in MDM
why: Protects data if device is lost or stolen

question: Do you have a Mobile Device Management (MDM) system managing all company devices?
fix: Jamf (Mac), Intune (Microsoft), Kandji, Mosyle
why: Allows remote wipe, policy enforcement, visibility

question: Are operating systems and software kept up to date with automatic updates enforced?
fix: Enforce via MDM; never allow staff to defer patches
why: Unpatched systems are the #1 exploit entry point

question: Do you have a documented policy for personal devices accessing company systems (BYOD)?
fix: Define acceptable use; enforce MDM enrolment for BYOD
why: Personal devices often lack corporate security controls

question: Do you have a documented process if a device is lost, stolen, or compromised?
fix: Written runbook: who to call, how to wipe, how to report
why: Without a plan, response is slow and inconsistent

question: Can you remotely wipe a lost or stolen device within 1 hour?
fix: MDM remote wipe capability; test this quarterly
why: Speed of wipe determines data exposure window

question: Do you have a policy preventing employees from installing unapproved software?
fix: Enforce application allowlist via MDM
why: Unapproved software is a major malware vector

question: Are USB ports and removable media restricted or monitored on company devices?
fix: Block via MDM or EDR policy
why: USB exfiltration is underestimated in SMBs

question: Do you monitor endpoint health and get alerted if a device goes unpatched?
fix: MDM compliance dashboard; EDR health monitoring
why: Visibility gaps create silent vulnerabilities

question: Do you have a process for securely decommissioning old devices before disposal?
fix: Full wipe + factory reset; certificate of destruction
why: Old devices with company data are routinely sold/donated

question: Are company devices protected by screen lock with a maximum 5-minute idle timeout?
fix: Enforce via MDM policy
why: Unattended devices in offices or cafés are easy targets

question: Do you scan devices for vulnerabilities on at least a monthly schedule?
fix: Tenable.io, Intruder, or Qualys
why: Patch management only works if you know what's unpatched

question: Do you have detection for malware that evades traditional antivirus (e.g. fileless malware)?
fix: CrowdStrike Falcon, SentinelOne Singularity
why: Advanced attackers use memory-based techniques

question: Are all mobile devices (phones and tablets) used for work enrolled in MDM with a PIN or biometric lock?
fix: Enforce via Intune, Jamf, or Google Workspace MDM
why: Unmanaged mobile devices are the fastest-growing attack surface

question: Do you have an asset register listing every device with its owner, OS version, and last patch date?
fix: Maintained in MDM platform or a simple spreadsheet
why: You cannot secure assets you cannot enumerate

question: Are developer workstations treated with the same security controls as all other endpoints?
fix: Developers are high-value targets; apply EDR, MDM, and disk encryption
why: Developer machines hold source code, credentials, and production access

question: Do you isolate endpoints that are suspected of compromise from the network automatically or with a one-click workflow?
fix: EDR network isolation feature (CrowdStrike, SentinelOne)
why: Speed of isolation determines how far ransomware or attackers spread

question: Are your endpoints configured with application control or allowlisting to prevent execution of unknown binaries?
fix: Windows Defender Application Control (WDAC), Airlock Digital
why: Application control is Essential 8 Maturity Level 3 and stops most malware

question: Do you have host-based firewall rules configured on all endpoints in addition to the network firewall?
fix: Enforce via MDM; Windows Defender Firewall or macOS Application Firewall
why: Host firewall provides a last line of defence if network perimeter fails

question: Is browser security hardened on all endpoints (extensions restricted, dangerous settings disabled)?
fix: Browser hardening via MDM; block unapproved extensions
why: Browser is the most common initial access vector in modern attacks

question: Do you conduct at least annual red team or adversary simulation exercises against your endpoints?
fix: Engage a penetration tester; use tools like Atomic Red Team
why: Simulated attacks reveal gaps that scanners miss

question: Do you know where all your sensitive data lives — every system and storage service?
fix: Data mapping exercise; use a simple spreadsheet to start
why: You cannot protect what you cannot locate

question: Is sensitive data encrypted at rest in all storage systems?
fix: Enable encryption on RDS, S3, Google Drive, Dropbox
why: Encryption at rest is a baseline compliance requirement

question: Is sensitive data encrypted in transit (TLS enforced for all data movement)?
fix: Enforce HTTPS everywhere; use TLS 1.2 or higher
why: Unencrypted transit exposes data to interception

question: Do you back up critical data regularly and test restores within the last 90 days?
fix: 3-2-1 backup rule; test restore quarterly
why: Untested backups fail when you need them most

question: Are your cloud storage buckets and databases access-controlled with no public exposure?
fix: AWS S3 Block Public Access; GCS/Azure equivalent
why: Publicly exposed S3 buckets are a chronic breach cause

question: Do you have a data retention and deletion policy that is actively enforced?
fix: Define retention periods; automate deletion where possible
why: Retaining data longer than needed increases breach exposure

question: Do you know which third-party tools and vendors have access to your data?
fix: OAuth audit in Google Workspace/Microsoft 365 admin
why: Third-party access is a hidden and growing supply chain risk

question: Do you classify your data by sensitivity level (public, internal, confidential, restricted)?
fix: Create a simple data classification policy document
why: Classification drives appropriate control decisions

question: Do you have DLP controls that alert or block when sensitive data is sent externally?
fix: Google Workspace DLP, Microsoft Purview, Nightfall AI
why: Prevents accidental and intentional data leakage

question: Are production databases separated from development and test environments?
fix: Never use production data in dev/test; use anonymised data
why: Dev environments have weaker controls; don't mix data

question: Do you have a process for handling customer data requests (GDPR/CCPA access, deletion)?
fix: Documented workflow + assigned owner for data requests
why: Legal obligation in most jurisdictions; fines for non-compliance

question: Do you review third-party integrations that have access to your data at least annually?
fix: Audit OAuth tokens; revoke unused integrations
why: Abandoned integrations retain access indefinitely

question: Do you have logging and alerting for unusual data access patterns (e.g. bulk downloads)?
fix: CloudTrail, Datadog, or SIEM with anomaly detection
why: Insider threats and attackers often exfiltrate data slowly

question: Are database credentials stored securely — never hardcoded in code or config files?
fix: AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, or Doppler
why: Hardcoded credentials in code repos are a critical vulnerability

question: Do you have controls preventing sensitive data from being copied to personal or unapproved cloud services?
fix: MDM restrictions + DLP + employee policy
why: Shadow copy of sensitive data bypasses all your controls

question: Do you conduct regular data mapping exercises as your product and team evolves?
fix: Schedule quarterly data mapping reviews
why: Data flows change constantly as new tools are adopted

question: Do you have a formal data breach response procedure including notification steps?
fix: Documented plan with legal counsel review
why: Regulatory deadlines for notification are strict (72 hrs GDPR)

question: Have you reviewed your cloud provider's shared responsibility model and confirmed your obligations?
fix: AWS/Azure/GCP shared responsibility documentation review
why: Many SMBs wrongly assume cloud provider covers everything

question: Are cloud infrastructure accounts (AWS/Azure/GCP) protected with MFA and root account access restricted?
fix: Lock root/global admin; require MFA for all cloud console logins
why: Cloud console root access is the master key to your entire infrastructure

question: Do you have cloud security posture management (CSPM) tooling scanning for misconfigurations?
fix: AWS Security Hub, Microsoft Defender for Cloud, Wiz, Lacework
why: Misconfiguration is the #1 cause of cloud data breaches

question: Are cloud IAM roles and service account permissions reviewed and minimised at least quarterly?
fix: AWS IAM Access Analyzer; Azure AD access review
why: Cloud over-permissioning is ubiquitous and routinely exploited

question: Do you have immutable, offsite backups that cannot be deleted or encrypted by ransomware?
fix: AWS S3 Object Lock, Azure Immutable Blob, Backblaze B2 with object lock
why: Ransomware increasingly targets and deletes backup repositories first

question: Are your cloud workloads protected at runtime against container escape and kernel exploits?
fix: Falco (open source), Aqua Security, Sysdig Secure
why: Cloud-native attacks targeting container runtimes are increasing

question: Do you use private endpoints or VPC peering for inter-service communication rather than public internet?
fix: AWS PrivateLink, Azure Private Endpoint, GCP VPC Service Controls
why: Traffic traversing the public internet is exposed to interception and interception

question: Have you configured cloud-level threat detection (e.g. AWS GuardDuty, Azure Defender) in all regions?
fix: Enable GuardDuty/Defender with alerting to your SIEM
why: Cloud threat detection is often disabled by default and costs pennies to run

question: Do you have a process for rotating cloud access keys and certificates before they expire?
fix: Automate rotation via Secrets Manager; alert at 30-day expiry
why: Expired or leaked cloud keys are a persistent high-severity risk

question: Do all staff use a business email domain — no personal Gmail or Yahoo for work?
fix: Google Workspace or Microsoft 365 Business
why: Personal accounts bypass IT control and retention policies

question: Is your email domain protected against spoofing with SPF, DKIM, and DMARC configured?
fix: Configure DNS records; verify with MXToolbox.com
why: Prevents attackers from sending email as your domain

question: Do you have a firewall between your internal network and the internet?
fix: Business firewall (Cisco Meraki, Fortinet, pfSense)
why: Essential perimeter control; default block inbound

question: Is your corporate Wi-Fi separated from guest Wi-Fi on separate VLANs?
fix: Configure VLAN isolation in your router/access point
why: Guest devices should never reach internal systems

question: Do you use a VPN or zero-trust network access (ZTNA) for remote access to internal systems?
fix: Tailscale (easy), Cloudflare Access, Cisco AnyConnect
why: Remote access without VPN/ZTNA exposes internal systems

question: Do you monitor for suspicious login activity and alert on anomalies such as impossible travel?
fix: Enable alerts in Google Workspace, M365, or Okta
why: Compromised accounts often show unusual login patterns

question: Do you have email filtering in place that scans inbound mail for phishing and malicious attachments?
fix: Google Workspace Advanced Protection, Proofpoint Essentials
why: Phishing is the #1 breach entry point globally

question: Is outbound email monitored or filtered to prevent data exfiltration?
fix: Google DLP for Gmail, Microsoft Purview for M365
why: Email is the most common data exfiltration channel

question: Do you have DNS filtering in place to block access to known malicious domains?
fix: Cloudflare Gateway (free), Cisco Umbrella, DNSFilter
why: Blocks malware C2 communications and phishing sites

question: Are RDP and other remote access services blocked from public internet exposure?
fix: Block port 3389 at firewall; use VPN instead
why: Exposed RDP is actively scanned and exploited globally

question: Do you have network segmentation isolating sensitive systems from general employee access?
fix: VLAN segmentation; firewall rules between segments
why: Limits lateral movement if attacker gains network access

question: Do you monitor network traffic for unusual patterns or unexpected external connections?
fix: IDS/IPS or SIEM with network monitoring
why: Detects malware calling home to command-and-control servers

question: Have you performed an external network scan to identify publicly exposed services in the last 12 months?
fix: Shodan, Intruder, or external pen tester
why: Know what attackers see before they do

question: Do you have intrusion detection or prevention capabilities monitoring your network?
fix: Palo Alto, Snort (open source), or cloud-native IDS
why: Signature and anomaly-based detection for network threats

question: Is DMARC configured with a policy of p=quarantine or p=reject (not just p=none)?
fix: Update DNS DMARC record to p=quarantine then p=reject after testing
why: p=none provides zero protection; only p=reject stops domain spoofing

question: Are all internet-facing systems protected by TLS 1.2 or higher with weak cipher suites disabled?
fix: Test with SSL Labs; disable TLS 1.0/1.1 and weak ciphers
why: Deprecated TLS versions are exploitable by active network attackers

question: Do you have a process for identifying and decommissioning unused internet-facing ports and services?
fix: Monthly Shodan/external scan; firewall rule review
why: Every unnecessary open port is an attack opportunity

question: Is your VPN solution monitored for known vulnerabilities and patched within 48 hours of critical CVEs?
fix: Subscribe to vendor CVE alerts; patch VPN appliances as highest priority
why: VPN appliances are a primary ransomware group initial access vector

question: Do you use a Secure Web Gateway (SWG) or cloud proxy to inspect and control outbound employee web traffic?
fix: Zscaler Internet Access, Netskope, Cloudflare Gateway
why: SWG blocks malware downloads, data exfiltration, and C2 traffic

question: Do you have email link rewriting and time-of-click URL analysis to catch phishing links that change after delivery?
fix: Proofpoint URL Defense, Microsoft Safe Links, Mimecast
why: Attackers use benign URLs that redirect to malicious content after email delivery

question: Is your network architecture zero-trust — systems authenticate every request rather than trusting network location?
fix: Cloudflare Access, Zscaler ZPA, BeyondCorp model
why: Traditional VPN perimeter fails once an attacker is inside the network

question: Do you have BGP route monitoring or ASN alerts to detect DNS hijacking or BGP route injection targeting your domain?
fix: Cloudflare Radar, Oracle Dyn BGP, or Cisco Umbrella
why: DNS/BGP hijacking silently redirects your users to attacker infrastructure

question: Do you maintain an inventory of all software, libraries, and dependencies in your product?
fix: SBOM tools: Syft, OWASP Dependency-Track
why: You cannot patch what you don't know you're running

question: Do you have a process for tracking and patching known software vulnerabilities (CVEs) in your stack?
fix: Dependabot (GitHub), Snyk, or OWASP Dependency-Check
why: Known CVEs are the most exploited vulnerabilities

question: Are software dependencies scanned for vulnerabilities as part of your development process?
fix: Add Snyk or Dependabot to your CI/CD pipeline
why: Catching vulns in CI is far cheaper than in production

question: Do you review code for security vulnerabilities before it goes into production?
fix: SAST tools: Semgrep, SonarCloud, CodeQL (free on GitHub)
why: Static analysis catches common vulnerabilities automatically

question: Are API keys, passwords, and credentials stored in a vault — never hardcoded in code?
fix: AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Doppler, Infisical
why: Hardcoded secrets are the most common AI/code leak vector

question: Do you scan code repositories for accidentally committed secrets or credentials?
fix: Trufflehog, GitGuardian, GitHub Secret Scanning
why: 29M secrets were leaked via public GitHub in 2025 alone

question: Do you have a process for evaluating the security of open-source libraries before adopting them?
fix: Check CVE database, GitHub activity, and maintainership
why: Abandoned or malicious packages are a growing supply chain risk

question: Do you have application-layer logging and alerting for unusual behaviour?
fix: Datadog APM, AWS CloudWatch, or self-hosted logging
why: Application anomalies are often the first sign of compromise

question: Are your production applications protected by a web application firewall (WAF)?
fix: Cloudflare WAF (easy, affordable), AWS WAF
why: WAF blocks OWASP Top 10 attacks like SQL injection and XSS

question: Do you conduct regular penetration testing or vulnerability assessments of your applications?
fix: Annual external pen test; automated scan tools quarterly
why: Pen tests find what automated scanners miss

question: Do you have a software bill of materials (SBOM) documenting all product components and versions?
fix: Syft, CycloneDX, or SPDX format
why: SBOM is becoming a regulatory and enterprise customer requirement

question: Do you have a vulnerability disclosure or bug bounty program for external security researchers?
fix: HackerOne, Bugcrowd, or self-hosted responsible disclosure
why: External researchers find real vulnerabilities before attackers

question: Is branch protection enabled on your main/production code branches, requiring peer review before merging?
fix: Enable branch protection in GitHub/GitLab with required approvals
why: Unreviewed code deployments introduce vulnerabilities and backdoors

question: Are container images scanned for vulnerabilities before deployment to production?
fix: Trivy, Grype, Snyk Container, or AWS ECR scanning
why: Container images frequently contain known vulnerable base OS packages

question: Do you have runtime application self-protection (RASP) or anomaly detection for your production APIs?
fix: Datadog AAP, Contrast Security, or AWS Lambda Insights
why: API abuse is the fastest-growing attack surface for SaaS products

question: Are third-party JavaScript libraries loaded in your web app monitored for supply chain compromise?
fix: Subresource Integrity (SRI) hashes; avoid CDN-loaded third-party scripts
why: Magecart and similar attacks inject malicious JS via compromised CDNs

question: Do your APIs enforce rate limiting, authentication, and input validation on every endpoint?
fix: API gateway (AWS API GW, Kong, Apigee); validate all inputs with schema
why: Unauthenticated or rate-unlimited APIs are trivially abused

question: Have you completed an OWASP Top 10 assessment for your primary customer-facing application?
fix: Self-assess using OWASP Top 10 checklist; engage pen tester annually
why: OWASP Top 10 covers the most exploited web vulnerability classes

question: Do you have dynamic application security testing (DAST) running against your staging environment?
fix: OWASP ZAP (free), Burp Suite Pro, or StackHawk in CI/CD
why: DAST finds runtime issues that static analysis cannot detect

question: Are cryptographic algorithms in your product restricted to approved modern ciphers (AES-256, SHA-256+, RSA-2048+)?
fix: Audit code and config for MD5, SHA-1, DES, or RC4; replace immediately
why: Deprecated cryptography is actively breakable by well-resourced attackers

question: Do you maintain a list of all AI tools your team uses — including shadow AI adopted without approval?
fix: Run a self-reporting survey; cross-check browser extensions
why: Most companies have 3-5x more AI tools than IT knows about

question: Do you have a policy governing what data employees can input into AI tools like ChatGPT or Claude?
fix: Written AI usage policy; include in onboarding and training
why: Employees routinely paste sensitive data into AI tools

question: Are AI tools that process customer or sensitive data formally reviewed before adoption?
fix: Create a lightweight AI tool intake review checklist
why: Unapproved AI tools may train on your data or leak it

question: Do you have controls preventing sensitive data from being submitted to external AI services?
fix: DLP rules for AI endpoints; browser extension blockers
why: Data sent to AI APIs may be logged, retained, or trained on

question: If you use AI agents with access to company systems, are their permissions documented and limited?
fix: Apply least privilege to AI agents as you would human users
why: AI agents with excess permissions are an ungoverned insider threat

question: Do you have logging and monitoring for AI agent actions — can you audit what an agent did and when?
fix: Require full audit log before enabling any AI agent
why: Ungoverned AI agents are the fastest-growing identity risk in 2026

question: Do you have an incident response plan covering AI-specific failures like prompt injection or agent misbehaviour?
fix: Add AI failure modes to your existing IR playbooks
why: Standard IR playbooks do not cover AI-specific attack vectors

question: Have you assessed the security posture of your AI providers — do they have SOC 2 or equivalent?
fix: Review vendor security pages and request SOC 2 reports
why: AI providers handle your queries and sometimes your data

question: Do you have an approved list of AI coding assistants and have communicated rules for their use with developers?
fix: Policy covering GitHub Copilot, Cursor, Claude Code — document what code can be shared
why: AI coding tools can leak proprietary algorithms and credentials to external AI providers

question: Have you tested your AI-integrated systems for prompt injection vulnerabilities?
fix: Manual red team testing; OWASP LLM Top 10 checklist
why: Prompt injection is the most prevalent AI attack vector and trivially exploitable

question: Do you have controls preventing AI tools from accessing production databases or customer records directly?
fix: Network segmentation; AI tools access read-only replicas or APIs only
why: AI tools with direct DB access can exfiltrate all customer data via carefully crafted queries

question: Are employees trained specifically on AI-powered social engineering attacks (deepfake audio/video, AI phishing)?
fix: Include AI threat scenarios in security awareness training
why: AI-generated phishing outperforms human-written phishing by 40% in click rates

question: Do you have a policy governing the use of AI-generated content in customer communications and marketing?
fix: Require human review of all AI-generated external communications
why: Unreviewed AI content creates legal, reputational, and misinformation risk

question: If you build AI/ML models, do you have controls protecting training data and model weights from exfiltration?
fix: Restrict model access to authorised systems; monitor for bulk export
why: Trained model weights represent significant IP and can be exploited by adversaries

question: Have you assessed your exposure to AI model supply chain attacks (e.g. malicious Hugging Face models, poisoned weights)?
fix: Use only models from verified sources; hash-verify downloads
why: Malicious model weights are an emerging supply chain attack vector

question: Do you have a process for evaluating and governing the use of autonomous AI agents that take actions on behalf of employees?
fix: Require security review before deploying any agentic workflow with write access
why: Autonomous agents amplify errors and attacks — one compromised agent can affect thousands of records

question: Do you have a formal process for evaluating vendor security posture before granting access?
fix: Use a standard security questionnaire (SIG Lite or custom)
why: Third parties are responsible for a significant % of breaches

question: Do you require key vendors to provide SOC 2, ISO 27001, or equivalent certification?
fix: Request certificates; check trust portals (e.g. security.vendor.com)
why: Certification is evidence of sustained security practice

question: Do you maintain a list of all third-party vendors with access to your systems and review it annually?
fix: Vendor register spreadsheet; review at least annually
why: Forgotten vendor access accumulates significant risk over time

question: Do vendor contracts include security requirements, data handling, and breach notification clauses?
fix: Have legal counsel review standard vendor contract template
why: Without contractual obligations vendors have no accountability

question: Do you monitor for security incidents affecting your key vendors or software providers?
fix: Subscribe to vendor security bulletins; monitor HaveIBeenPwned
why: Vendor breaches can silently affect your own security posture

question: Do you have a process for promptly revoking vendor access if the relationship ends or a breach is suspected?
fix: Include in offboarding checklist; tie to vendor register
why: Vendor access without review is equivalent to an open door

question: Have you assessed the security of your software supply chain — the open-source libraries your product depends on?
fix: Dependabot, Snyk, or OWASP Dependency-Track
why: Supply chain attacks via open-source packages are accelerating

question: Do you have contingency plans if a critical vendor suffers an outage or security incident?
fix: Document backup vendors or manual fallback processes
why: Third-party downtime caused by attacks can halt your operations

question: Do you check whether your critical SaaS providers have experienced data breaches using breach monitoring services?
fix: HaveIBeenPwned, SpyCloud, or Recorded Future for vendor monitoring
why: A breached vendor credential can expose your environment without any action by you

question: Do you have a tiered vendor risk classification (critical, high, medium, low) driving proportionate oversight?
fix: Categorise vendors by data access and business criticality; apply tiered reviews
why: Treating all vendors the same wastes resources and leaves critical vendors under-scrutinised

question: Are you notified automatically when a vendor in your stack discloses a CVE in their product?
fix: Subscribe to vendor CVE feeds; use tools like VulnDB or Feedly security feeds
why: Vendor CVEs affecting your deployed versions require rapid response

question: Have you assessed your exposure to typosquatting attacks on package managers (npm, PyPI, Maven)?
fix: Private package mirrors; namespace protection in npm/PyPI
why: Attackers publish malicious packages with names one character off legitimate ones

question: Do your build pipelines verify checksums or signatures of all external dependencies before use?
fix: Sigstore, in-toto attestations, or hash pinning in lock files
why: A compromised CDN or package registry can silently modify your build artifacts

question: Is your CI/CD pipeline itself secured — are pipeline secrets isolated and build agents not shared with untrusted code?
fix: Separate build agents per trust boundary; use OIDC for CI secrets
why: Compromised CI/CD can inject malicious code into every release

question: Do you have a written information security policy reviewed in the last 12 months?
fix: Start with free templates from SANS or CIS
why: A policy signals intent and provides legal protection

question: Have all employees completed security awareness training in the last 12 months?
fix: KnowBe4, Proofpoint PSAT, or free SANS resources
why: Human error causes 90%+ of breaches; training is the fix

question: Do you have a documented incident response plan tested or reviewed in the last year?
fix: Tabletop exercise with leadership team; annual review
why: Untested IR plans fail under the stress of a real incident

question: Do you conduct background checks on employees with access to sensitive data or systems?
fix: Background check services: Checkr, Sterling
why: Insider threat risk is underestimated in growing companies

question: Do you have cyber liability insurance and understand what it covers and excludes?
fix: Engage a specialist broker: Coalition, At-Bay, or Chubb
why: Cyber insurance is essential but exclusions matter enormously

question: Do you know your regulatory compliance obligations — HIPAA, SOC 2, GDPR, PCI DSS, or others?
fix: Consult a compliance advisor for your industry and geography
why: Ignorance of requirements does not reduce legal liability

question: Do you run phishing simulations to test whether employees can identify phishing emails?
fix: KnowBe4, Proofpoint, or free tools like GoPhish
why: Training without testing gives false confidence

question: Do you have a process for employees to report suspicious emails or security concerns — and is it actively used?
fix: Dedicated email alias + Slack channel + regular reminders
why: Under-reporting delays incident response and worsens outcomes

question: Is there a named individual responsible for information security decisions in your organisation?
fix: Assign a Security Owner role even if part-time; document it
why: Without ownership, security initiatives stall and accountability is absent

question: Do you conduct at least annual tabletop exercises simulating a ransomware or data breach scenario with your leadership team?
fix: Facilitated 2-hour tabletop; use CISA or NCSC scenario templates
why: Leadership response during an incident determines outcome; tabletops reveal gaps before they matter

question: Do you have a clear escalation path and communication plan for notifying customers and regulators after a breach?
fix: Pre-draft notification templates; identify regulatory contacts in advance
why: Ad-hoc breach communication under pressure leads to compliance failures and reputational damage

question: Are security metrics reported to the board or executive team at least quarterly?
fix: Simple KPI dashboard: open threats, compliance score, incidents, training completion
why: Security without board visibility is underfunded and deprioritised

question: Have you assessed whether your current security controls meet the requirements of your largest customers or prospects?
fix: Review customer security questionnaires received; map gaps to your controls
why: Enterprise customers will not sign contracts without evidence of adequate controls

question: Do you maintain a risk register documenting identified security risks, owners, and accepted/mitigated status?
fix: Simple spreadsheet risk register; review quarterly
why: A risk register is required by ISO 27001, SOC 2, and most enterprise procurement questionnaires

question: Do you have a documented business continuity plan that covers a ransomware or major cyberattack scenario?
fix: NCSC/CISA BCP templates; tabletop to validate
why: Ransomware attacks now have a median dwell time of under 24 hours — plans must exist before the event

question: Do you maintain offline or air-gapped backups of your most critical data that are inaccessible to ransomware?
fix: Tape, offline disk, or immutable cloud storage (S3 Object Lock)
why: Connected backups are encrypted in 80% of ransomware attacks

question: Have you tested restoration from backup within the last 6 months for your most critical systems?
fix: Schedule semi-annual restore test; document recovery time achieved
why: Unverified backup recovery times are almost always longer than assumed

question: Do you know your Recovery Time Objective (RTO) and Recovery Point Objective (RPO) for each critical system?
fix: Define RTO/RPO per system; validate against backup and DR capability
why: Without defined RTOs, recovery prioritisation fails under pressure

question: Do you have cyber incident retainer or pre-negotiated support from a cybersecurity incident response firm?
fix: CrowdStrike Services, Mandiant, or regional IR firm retainer
why: Finding and engaging an IR firm during an active attack costs hours you cannot afford

question: Are your backups tested to confirm they are not also encrypted or corrupted by ransomware before relying on them?
fix: Verify backup integrity with checksum validation; use immutable backup storage
why: Ransomware increasingly lurks for weeks corrupting backups before triggering encryption

question: Do you have a communication plan for customers, staff, and press in the event of a ransomware attack?
fix: Pre-draft customer notification email; identify press spokesperson
why: Ransomware victims are judged as much on communication quality as on the incident itself

question: Do you have an out-of-band communication channel (e.g. personal phones, WhatsApp group) for the response team if email is unavailable?
fix: Pre-establish personal contact list for incident team
why: Ransomware often locks email and collaboration platforms during an attack

question: Have you identified which systems, if encrypted, would halt your business entirely — and do you have a recovery priority list?
fix: Map critical path systems; prioritise ERP, comms, auth, and customer data
why: Prioritised recovery saves days of recovery time in a real attack

question: Do you have a policy decision made on whether you would pay a ransomware demand — and have you discussed this with legal counsel?
fix: Board-level decision in advance; understand OFAC sanction implications
why: Deciding under pressure with lawyers on the phone is extremely costly and slow

question: Can you continue to pay employees and suppliers if your finance systems are encrypted for 2 weeks?
fix: Maintain offline copy of bank details and payroll; secondary payment method
why: Ransomware victims have failed to make payroll; this causes staff attrition mid-crisis

question: Do you have a documented checklist of all accounts, credentials, and access tokens that need to be rotated after a breach?
fix: Pre-built post-incident credential rotation checklist
why: Incomplete credential rotation after an incident leads to re-compromise within weeks

question: Are your backups stored in a separate cloud account or geography that cannot be reached from your production environment?
fix: Cross-account S3 replication; Azure Backup vault in separate subscription
why: Single-account backups are wiped in 100% of sophisticated ransomware attacks that reach cloud infra

question: Have you performed a full DR failover test — not just a backup restore — to validate you can run operations from a secondary environment?
fix: Annual DR exercise; measure actual RTO against objective
why: Backup restoration is necessary but not sufficient; full failover testing is the gold standard

question: Do you have canary files or honeypot indicators that alert you if ransomware begins encrypting your file shares?
fix: Canary tokens (canarytokens.org) in shared drives; EDR honeypot files
why: Ransomware canaries provide 10–60 minutes of early warning before encryption completes

question: Is your incident response retainer tested — have you onboarded your IR firm and shared access credentials with them before an incident?
fix: Pre-share access credentials; run a non-emergency contact exercise annually
why: Untested retainers add 4-8 hours of friction at the worst possible time

question: Do you have business interruption insurance that covers revenue loss from a cyber incident?
fix: Confirm cyber policy covers BI loss; many SMB policies exclude it
why: BI loss is often the largest financial impact of ransomware, exceeding recovery costs

question: Have you mapped which regulatory notifications are required and within what timeframes if you suffer a ransomware event?
fix: Australian Privacy Act notifiable breach provisions; sector-specific requirements
why: Notification deadlines run from discovery, not from resolution — you must act while still in crisis

question: Do you have network segmentation specifically designed to prevent ransomware from spreading beyond its initial point of compromise?
fix: Micro-segmentation; isolate file shares from workstations; block SMB between endpoints
why: Flat networks allow ransomware to encrypt all endpoints and shares within minutes

question: Do you have an executive crisis management process separate from your technical IR process, with a dedicated decision-maker?
fix: Assign an Incident Commander role; run a leadership tabletop
why: Technical IR and executive crisis management must run in parallel but have different decision rights

question: Is access to your office or workplace restricted to authorised personnel using key cards, PIN, or similar?
fix: Electronic access control (HID, Brivo, Kisi); remove shared keys
why: Physical access enables device theft, shoulder surfing, and direct system compromise

question: Do you have a visitor log and escort policy for non-employees entering areas with sensitive systems?
fix: Visitor register; require staff escort in server/IT areas
why: Unescorted visitors can physically access systems, plant devices, or observe screens

question: Are server rooms, network equipment, and storage systems physically secured with restricted access?
fix: Locked cage or room; audit trail of access
why: Physical access to servers bypasses all logical security controls

question: Are employees trained to challenge and report tailgating through secure doors?
fix: Include in security awareness training; post signage at access points
why: Social engineering via physical tailgating bypasses expensive electronic access control

question: Do employees use a privacy screen on laptops when working in public places like cafés or airports?
fix: Issue privacy screens via IT; include in travel security policy
why: Visual eavesdropping is low-tech, cheap, and effective — credentials and data are routinely stolen this way

question: Is there a clean desk policy requiring sensitive documents and screens to be secured when unattended?
fix: Policy + reminders; include in onboarding
why: Unattended documents and unlocked screens are a primary source of physical data exposure

question: Do you have CCTV covering physical access points to server rooms and sensitive areas?
fix: IP cameras with 30-day retention; monitoring alerts
why: CCTV deters and provides evidence for physical security incidents

question: Are physical access logs reviewed at least monthly to identify anomalous entry patterns?
fix: Export access control logs; review for after-hours or unusual entries
why: Physical access anomalies often precede insider incidents

question: Do you have a policy and process for securely destroying physical media (paper, hard drives, USB drives) containing sensitive data?
fix: Cross-cut shredder; certified hard drive destruction; document with certificates
why: Dumpster diving and drive recovery are real and underestimated attack vectors

question: Are employees instructed never to plug in unknown USB drives or devices found in the workplace?
fix: Include in security training; cover USB drop attack scenarios
why: USB drop attacks have a 45-98% success rate in studies; one plug can compromise an entire network

question: Do you have a travel security policy covering international travel with company devices to high-risk countries?
fix: Loaner devices for high-risk travel; VPN required; customs inspection awareness
why: Devices can be legally inspected or covertly compromised at borders in many jurisdictions

question: Are public-facing network ports (Ethernet jacks in meeting rooms, lobbies) disabled when not in use?
fix: Disable unused switch ports via 802.1X or manual disable
why: Enabled network ports in accessible areas allow attackers to plug in and access internal network

question: Do you have a process for reporting and responding to suspected physical security breaches (lost key card, forced entry)?
fix: Report to IT/security immediately; revoke lost access credentials within 1 hour
why: A lost key card that is not revoked is equivalent to a stolen password that is not changed

question: Do you have controls to prevent or detect rogue wireless access points or network devices being installed on your premises?
fix: Wi-Fi scanning tools; 802.1X network authentication; periodic physical sweeps
why: Rogue APs are used for man-in-the-middle attacks and corporate espionage

question: Are building systems (HVAC, BMS, access control, CCTV) isolated from your IT network and secured separately?
fix: OT/IT network segmentation; patch BMS systems on their own schedule
why: Compromised building management systems have been used to gain initial network access

question: Do you have a documented process for maintaining security posture during office moves, renovations, or major facility changes?
fix: Security checklist for facility transitions; include IT and physical security teams
why: Office moves are a common time for access controls to be misconfigured or overlooked

question: Have you conducted a physical penetration test or red team exercise within the last 2 years?
fix: Engage a physical pen tester; scope to include social engineering and tailgating
why: Physical controls are rarely tested; real gaps are almost always found in first assessment

question: Do you have an insider threat program that includes behavioural indicators for both physical and digital anomalies?
fix: Define insider threat indicators; train managers; create anonymous reporting channel
why: Insider threats combine physical and digital actions; isolated detection misses the full picture

question: Is critical infrastructure (internet uplinks, power supply, cooling) protected against both physical attack and natural disaster?
fix: Dual ISP; UPS; colocation backup; generator test annually
why: Physical disruption of infrastructure can be used to force failover to less-secure systems

question: Do you have controls preventing employees from working on sensitive data in areas where screens can be recorded by security cameras or external windows?
fix: Screen orientation policy; privacy screens in open-plan offices; window film
why: Surveillance of screens by cameras (including smartphone cameras) is a growing corporate espionage vector
